versions.short: The bill would change federal college rules to help students with disabilities. Colleges receiving federal aid would have to accept several kinds of existing paperwork, such as high school education plans, disability plans, or records from licensed professionals, as proof that a student has a disability. Schools would also have to explain clearly how they decide what accommodations students can receive and share that information publicly. Colleges would further have to report yearly counts and percentages of students registered with disability services, with exceptions where individual students could be identified. The bill would also authorize $10,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for a national center that supports disabled postsecondary students. It would leave the meanings of reasonable accommodation under existing disability laws unchanged.
